title: Native inquest halted over jury challenge
article: Pre-inquest proceedings ground to a halt yesterday in the coroner's probe of the death of two First Nations men killed in a jail fire in Ontario's far north almost three years ago.

An inquest was scheduled to begin Oct. 20 in Cochrane into the deaths of Ricardo Wesley and James Goodwin, both 20, who were burned to death in a Jan. 8, 2006 fire at the lone police lockup on the Kashechewan First Nation, located on the shores of James Bay.

But presiding coroner Dr. David Eden adjourned the hearing indefinitely yesterday after the issue of the validity of the jury rolls in the vast judicial territory of Kenora -- where Cochrane is located -- was raised by Julian Falconer, one of two lawyers representing the Wesleys.

"The family has brought to the attention of the coroner that the jury roll in the District of Kenora is not legally valid," Falconer said after the hearing concluded. "The proceedings had to be adjourned while the coroner's office gets a legal opinion from the ministry of the attorney general."
The Wesley and Goodwin families are both seeking to have the inquest moved out of Cochrane and into a larger venue where it would get more public attention.
The Wesleys have already persuaded Eden to include the issues of First Nations police training, funding and the overall adequacy of First Nations police services.
